newsitem.title: USA: Day two of Oklahoma City bomb deliberations begins.
newsitem.headline: Day two of Oklahoma City bomb deliberations begins.

text.p: Jurors in the trial of accused Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh arrived at the federal courthouse in Denver on Saturday to begin their second day of deliberations, court sources said.
The jury of seven men and five women arrived at the courthouse in two vans with darkened windows, eyewitnesses said.
Court officials would not confirm if deliberations had begun.
The jury spent nearly a full day on Friday weighing the fate of McVeigh, who is accused of blowing up the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995, killing 168 people.
The Gulf War veteran, 29, has pleaded not guilty to charges of conspiracy, bombing and the first-degree murder of eight federal agents killed in the blast.

The jury heard from more than 160 witnesses during five weeks of testimony in the high-profile trial. Federal Judge Richard Matsch on Friday admonished the jurors not to discuss the case outside of deliberations at the court.
